message.content:
During the 19th century the world’s most celebrated sculpture was **“The Kiss”** by Auguste Rodin (1889).  
It captured the era’s fascination with realism, emotion, and the human form, and it became an icon of modern art.  

Other notable 19th‑century masterpieces include:

| Artist | Sculpture | Year |
|--------|-----------|------|
| Auguste Rodin | “The Gates of Hell” (series) | 1880–1895 |
| Antonio Canova | “Psyche Revived by Cupid’s Kiss” (reworked) | 1793–1808 (still influential into the 19th c.) |
| Jean-Baptiste Léonard | “La Marseillaise” (statue) | 1830 |
| John Steuart Parker | “The Angel of the North” (not actually built until 2007, but the design concept dates back to the 19th c.) | — |

These works illustrate how sculpture evolved from neoclassical ideals toward more expressive, naturalistic forms that defined the artistic landscape of the 19th century.
